name: two-column-report
title: Two-column report
blurb: Five pages set in two columns, drawn row by row as many exporters do.
shows: A plain text parser joins the halves of different sentences. A layout parser reads each column in turn. Two questions are planted to miss: one fact lives only in a page footer, and one answer is ranked too low to be checked.

teaches.question: fieldwork
teaches.why: The answer is only in page 3's footer, and Docling sets page footers aside by default.
teaches.fix_text: In Parse, read page headers and footers too (Docling's content_layers).

teaches.question: most-gain
teaches.why: The question shares few words with the answer, and many paragraphs about the twelve documents look alike, so the right piece comes back below the 5 checked.
teaches.fix_text: Add the cross-encoder reranker, which reads the question and each piece together.

teaches.question: lost-place
teaches.why: The answer wraps inside the left column, and a plain text parser reads across both columns.
teaches.fix_text: Parse with Docling, which reads each column in turn.
